correctness.rationale: The two conjugated pinching maps are orthogonal projections with product equal to scalar depolarization, and they alternate because conjugation by the monomial square preserves the diagonal algebra. The moving-frame product therefore splits into orthogonal subspaces of dimensions 1, d−1, d−1, (d−1)^2 with factors 1, Qodd, Qeven, Qodd Qeven. The unitary right factor preserves all singular values. Hermitian perturbations pulled back through the inverse unitary verify physically attainable sharpness. The product inequality and equality conditions rigorously classify all optimal schedules. Direct matrix superoperator tests and an exact finite grid independently support boundary and sampled cases; infinite/continuous families are justified by the proof, not by numerical extrapolation.
risks: Any departure from complex-Hadamardness or monomial-square structure invalidates the two-algebra reduction; not claimed in scope.

value.rationale: Quantum-walk coherent/classical interpolation creates a motivated need for exact finite-time mixing under varying dephasing strengths. The theorem solves the full dimension-independent singular-spectrum problem, establishes a physically realizable sharp worst-state contraction, and completely classifies the global fixed-total-probability minimax schedules for every duration. The bang-bang two-parity allocation and optimizer rigidity are not merely the already known B=2 mutual-unbiased-measurement corollary. It gives a concrete, reusable control benchmark and sharp boundary of the Hadamard-monomial class.
risks: Utility is specific to Hilbert–Schmidt contraction and sum-of-probabilities cost, not a universal physical dephasing energy model.
